extracted.intended_audience: suppliers/contractors bidding on US Indian Service procurements; procurement officials and historians
extracted.subtask_description: Abstract of proposals received and contracts awarded (advertisement May 10, 1880) for supplies to the U.S. Indian Service, listing item specifications, quantities, units, points of delivery, quoted rates, footnoted conditions, and notes on awards. Used to interpret how contracts were evaluated and awarded.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sample submission requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Awards were made on comparison of samples with which each bid was accompanied.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Every bid must be accompanied by a physical sample. Contract award decisions were based on comparing those samples (i.e., quality/finish of the sample) across bidders; presence/quality of the sample is an explicit evaluation input.

rubrics_metrics.name: Awarded-rate notation
rubrics_metrics.description: Figures in large type denote the rates at which contracts have been awarded.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When reading the report, large-type figures indicate the winning (awarded) unit rates. This is how to distinguish awarded prices from other quoted proposals in the table.

rubrics_metrics.name: Item specification compliance (material, finish, construction)
rubrics_metrics.description: Each line-item includes required material, construction, finish, or treatment (e.g., 'Pans, fry, wrought-iron, polished'; 'Pans, dish, stamped, retinned, 10-quart'; 'Plates, tin, dinner, stamped').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Bidders must supply goods matching the listed specification terms (material, stamped/retinned/polished, quart/inch sizes, etc.). The item text functions as a technical specification to be met exactly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Units, quantities, and unit-pricing
rubrics_metrics.description: Items are specified with units and quantities (dozen, pounds, gross, per piece) and prices are quoted per that unit (e.g., 'dozen', 'pounds', 'gross').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Bids must state per-unit rates corresponding to the stated unit. The table compares per-unit bids for identical units and quantities; awards are recorded as per-unit rates.

rubrics_metrics.name: Points of delivery / delivery-location pricing
rubrics_metrics.description: Points of delivery (cities/regions) are listed for each bid line and prices vary by delivery point.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A bidder's quoted rate is tied to a specific point(s) of delivery (e.g., New York, Chicago, Kansas City). Contract evaluation and awarded rates take delivery point into account; bidders must specify which delivery points they will serve and at what rate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conditional price adjustments (packaging, furniture, crates)
rubrics_metrics.description: Footnoted conditional pricing adjustments appear (examples: '15 per cent less if not crated.'; '$4.50 less without furniture').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Quoted prices may be adjusted downward depending on packaging or optional components; bidders and readers must apply footnote conditions when comparing effective prices. Footnotes indicate how to compute alternate pricing scenarios.

rubrics_metrics.name: Quality grades and finish requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Some items include explicit quality grades or finish notes (e.g., 'best steel amalgam', '2d quality', 'retinned', 'polished').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Bids must match the specified quality grade or finish; comparisons are among samples/quotes of the same declared quality grade. Lower/higher quality grades are marked and treated separately.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dimensional and variant footnotes
rubrics_metrics.description: Footnotes specify exact dimensions or variant measurements for certain items (examples: 'e 31 inches. / 30 inches. g 38 inches.'; other notes denoting cylinder inches, oven sizes, etc.).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Bidders must conform to the footnoted dimensions/variants; evaluators use these footnotes to ensure like-for-like comparisons. Where sizes vary, separate quantities or pricing may apply.

rubrics_metrics.name: Manufacturer / source specification or disclosure
rubrics_metrics.description: Some bids or entries note the manufacturer/source of goods (example: 'All iron on this bid manufactured by L. Oliver & Phillips, of Pittsburgh').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Manufacturer identity may be recorded or required; origin/manufacturer information can be a factor in evaluation or acceptance and is documented in the report.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evaluation factors: combined price and sample quality
rubrics_metrics.description: Contract awards reflect a combination of the submitted sample quality and the quoted rate (price); both were used to decide awards.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Neither price alone nor sample alone determined awards—awards were made by comparing quality of samples and the bidder's rate together. Interpreters should assess both factors when reconstructing award rationale.

rubrics_metrics.name: Categorization by class and itemization
rubrics_metrics.description: Items are organized by class headings (e.g., 'Class 17. Tin and stamped ware', 'Class 18. Stoves, Hollow Ware, Tin, &c.', 'HARDWARE') with line-itemized specifications beneath.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Bidders and evaluators should refer to class-level grouping to find applicable items and specifications; class headings define procurement categories and scope for bids.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notation of packaging, delivery terms, and per-location delivery conditions
rubrics_metrics.description: Besides points of delivery, the document contains notes such as 'Delivered in Chicago', 'Delivered in New York', and other delivery/packing conditions that affect pricing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Delivery terms (where accepted delivered) are material contractual conditions and must be observed in pricing comparisons; reads of awarded rates should account for where delivery is to occur.
